boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain The University of Tennessee-Knoxville
boards.description: Ten currently documented late-evening food and campus destinations on or immediately beside UT Knoxville’s main campus.

cards.title: Raising Cane's Cumberland Ave
cards.subtitle: 1830 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Check the order counter or pickup options before heading over; the official location lists late food-service and dine-in hours every day.
cards.short_summary: A Cumberland Avenue chicken-finger stop with service extending into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane’s lists this 1830 Cumberland Avenue location as open until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 4:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; dine-in runs until 2 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: food service until 3 a.m. Sun–Wed and 4:30 a.m. Thu–Sat; dine-in until 2 a.m. daily. Confirm holiday changes before going.

cards.title: Gus's Good Times Deli
cards.subtitle: 815 Melrose Place, near the UT Strip
cards.notes: Use the deli’s posted schedule to time a sandwich pickup, especially on weeknights when its closing time differs from the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A long-running UT Strip deli with late posted hours and delivery availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Gus’s lists hours until 2 a.m. Monday–Wednesday, 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday, and 12:01 a.m. Sunday at 815 Melrose Place.
cards.access_notes: Official posted hours: Mon–Wed until 2 a.m.; Thu–Sat until 3 a.m.; Sun until 12:01 a.m. Check the site for changes.

cards.title: Cook Out
cards.subtitle: 2135 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Choose walk-up, drive-thru, or seating as available, and verify the current closing time before making the short trip from campus.
cards.short_summary: A Cumberland Avenue fast-food destination with hours reaching early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Apple Maps lists Cook Out at 2135 Cumberland Avenue with hours until 4 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 5 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Apple Maps — Cook Out, 2135 Cumberland Ave
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 10:30 a.m.–4 a.m. Sun–Thu and 10:30 a.m.–5 a.m. Fri–Sat. Check live business information before departing.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: 2121 Cumberland Avenue, Suite 103
cards.notes: Plan a cookie pickup around the listed late closing schedule; Thursday through Saturday have the latest posted availability.
cards.short_summary: A dessert counter on Cumberland Avenue with late-night hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Waze lists Insomnia Cookies at 2121 Cumberland Avenue as open until 1 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and until 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: until 1 a.m. Sun–Wed and until 3 a.m. Thu–Sat. Confirm the live listing, including pickup availability, before visiting.

cards.title: Subway
cards.subtitle: 2104 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Order ahead or walk in for a sandwich; check the official store page for the day’s late closing time before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A sandwich shop on Cumberland Avenue with daily hours extending past 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Subway’s official page lists its 2104 Cumberland Avenue restaurant open until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official store hours: until 3 a.m. Sun–Wed and 3:30 a.m. Thu–Sat. Check the location page for temporary schedule changes.

cards.title: Mellow Mushroom Knoxville
cards.subtitle: 2109 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use the official store schedule when planning a later pizza meal; Friday and Saturday have the latest posted closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Cumberland Avenue pizza restaurant open until 11 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Mellow Mushroom lists its 2109 Cumberland Avenue location open until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Sun–Thu and 11 a.m.–11 p.m. Fri–Sat. Verify holiday and event-day changes before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Moe's Southwest Grill University of Tennessee
cards.title: Moe's Southwest Grill University of Tennessee
cards.subtitle: 1800 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Keep this option in mind for an evening burrito or bowl, and check the store page if campus events could affect regular hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge Tex-Mex restaurant with a posted 10 p.m. close every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Moe’s official location page lists the University of Tennessee restaurant at 1800 Cumberland Avenue open from 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Moe's Southwest Grill — University of Tennessee
cards.access_notes: Official posted hours are 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m. daily. Confirm the location page for exceptions before visiting.

cards.title: Rocky Top Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: UT Knoxville campus
cards.notes: Check the current dining schedule before walking over; the published dinner period provides a campus-based option on several late evenings.
cards.short_summary: A UT dining hall with dinner service listed until 10 p.m. on Sunday through Thursday.
cards.evidence_claim: Vol Dining lists Rocky Top Dining Hall dinner until 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday; Friday and Saturday dinner ends at 8 p.m.
cards.source_title: Vol Dining — Rocky Top Dining Hall
cards.access_notes: Published dinner hours are 4:30–10 p.m. Mon–Thu and Sun, and 4:30–8 p.m. Fri–Sat. Check the live dining calendar for break-period changes.

cards.title: Cumberland Food Hall
cards.subtitle: Hub Knoxville, Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use this multi-vendor stop for an early-evening meal near campus, and review Vol Dining’s live listings before heading across the Strip.
cards.short_summary: A Vol Dining food hall on Cumberland Avenue with nightly service listed through 9 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Vol Dining states that Cumberland Food Hall operates from 10:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. seven days a week, excluding major holidays.
cards.source_title: Vol Dining Celebrates Grand Opening of Cumberland Food Hall
cards.access_notes: Vol Dining lists 10:30 a.m.–9 p.m. daily, excluding major holidays; check the current dining schedule for vendor-specific or break-period changes.

cards.title: Student Union
cards.subtitle: 1502 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use the building as a well-defined campus endpoint before 10 p.m.; confirm special schedules before relying on it during breaks or game days.
cards.short_summary: A central UT campus building whose academic-year facility hours extend to 10 p.m. most days.
cards.evidence_claim: UT lists Student Union academic-year facility hours until 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, and until 11 p.m. Friday.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year facility hours end at 10 p.m. most days and 11 p.m. Friday. Retail dining hours vary; the page advises checking special closures and break schedules.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Named, campus-based spaces for collaborative study, quiet work, media projects, and hands-on making.

cards.title: Commons Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library, second floor
cards.notes: Reserve a two-hour block online for a group session, or use the Commons’ conversational setting for a project check-in.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms in Hodges’ Learning Commons, including specialty rooms with presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists general-use study rooms in Commons North and South and states that online reservations may be made up to two weeks ahead, with a two-hour daily maximum.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are online only; consult UT Libraries for current building access and availability.

cards.title: Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library, third floor
cards.notes: Meet your group in one of the first-come rooms; bring your materials and choose a room sized for the work at hand.
cards.short_summary: First-come group study rooms on Hodges’ third floor, including larger rooms for bigger groups.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries identifies Hodges third-floor study rooms as group-study spaces that are not reservable and available first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable; use is first come, first served. Check current library access before visiting.

cards.title: Active Learning Space
cards.subtitle: Commons South, Hodges Library room 235
cards.notes: Shift from a seated study session to standing desks or pedal workstations when you want a different way to work.
cards.short_summary: An alternative study setup with standing-height desks, pedal laptop workstations, and balance chairs.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries describes the Active Learning Space in Commons South as a student study and assignment space outfitted with standing desks, pedal laptop workstations, and balance chairs.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hodges Library room 235; verify current library access and space availability.

cards.title: Medbery Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library rooms 209 and 211
cards.notes: Plan a small creative build and use the listed light-fabrication tools for a course or personal project.
cards.short_summary: A Hodges Library creative-work area with 3D printers, sewing machines, and Cricut vinyl cutters.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries states that the Medbery Makerspace is available for creative work and includes 3D printers, sewing machines, and Cricut vinyl cutters.
cards.access_notes: Located in rooms 209 and 211; check UT Libraries for current access guidance and equipment procedures.

cards.title: Media Production Studio
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library room 251
cards.notes: Reserve the studio for a video or photo assignment, then check in at the Studio desk in Commons South.
cards.short_summary: A reservable Hodges studio designed for video and photo projects.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries identifies the Media Production Studio in Hodges room 251 as a reservable space for video and photo projects and directs users to check in at the Studio desk.
cards.access_notes: Reservable; check in at the Studio desk in Commons South and confirm current reservation requirements.

cards.title: Audio Studios & Whisper Room
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library rooms 235E–G
cards.notes: Reserve a recording slot, check in at the Studio desk, and borrow the available microphone, headphones, or synth.
cards.short_summary: Three reservable audio-recording studios plus a vocal booth inside the Hodges Library Studio.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists three reservable Audio Recording Studios and a Whisper Room vocal booth, with microphone, headphone, and synth checkout at the Studio desk.
cards.access_notes: Reservable; users check in at the Studio desk. Confirm current reservation and equipment-loan rules.

cards.title: Studio Workstations
cards.subtitle: Commons South, Hodges Library room 235
cards.notes: Reserve a workstation or check in at the Studio desk when you need media and design software for a project.
cards.short_summary: Reservable media-and-design workstations with Adobe Creative Suite and equipment for varied media formats.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries states that Studio Workstations provide Adobe Creative Suite and input equipment for media formats and may be reserved or accessed through the Studio desk.
cards.access_notes: Reserve online or check in at the Studio desk; verify current workstation availability.

cards.title: eXperience Point Gaming Lab
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library room 253
cards.notes: Use the lab’s student-use setup for a gaming or work session, and check the library’s current rules before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A Hodges computer lab that UT Libraries says is open to students as a gaming or work space.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries describes the eXperience Point Gaming Lab in Hodges room 253 as a computer lab open for student use as a gaming space or work space.
cards.access_notes: Located in room 253; confirm current student-use hours and any equipment or lab rules with UT Libraries.

cards.title: Miles Reading Room Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library room 135
cards.notes: Book an enclosed room when your group needs more separation than the open Commons spaces provide.
cards.short_summary: Three reservable enclosed study rooms in Hodges’ Miles Reading Room.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries states that the Miles Reading Room has three reservable enclosed study rooms that are more private than Commons study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Reservable rooms in Hodges room 135; check the UT Libraries reservation system for availability.

cards.title: Brenda Lewis Peel Galleria
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library, second floor room 200
cards.notes: Pass through the central second-floor corridor and look for university or registered-student-organization information tables.
cards.short_summary: A central Hodges Library Galleria used for outreach and information tabling.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries describes the Brenda Lewis Peel Galleria as a central second-floor space and an information-tabling location for UT departments and student organizations.
cards.access_notes: Sales and solicitation are prohibited in library spaces; tabling is subject to UT Libraries policies.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission places and activities at UT and nearby Knoxville.

cards.title: Walk the UT Gardens
cards.subtitle: 2518 Jacob Drive, UT Knoxville
cards.notes: Take a self-guided walk among the garden displays; plan for ordinary public hours and skip special-ticketed events.
cards.short_summary: A sunrise-to-sunset botanical walk on the UT campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Gardens, Knoxville is open to the public seven days a week from sunrise to sunset, and admission is free except during some special events.
cards.access_notes: Free general admission; special events can have entry fees. Public hours are sunrise to sunset.

cards.entity_name: McClung Museum of Natural History & Culture
cards.title: Browse the McClung Museum
cards.subtitle: 1327 Circle Park Drive, UT Knoxville
cards.notes: Reserve ahead if preferred, then explore the current exhibitions and permanent collections during regular museum hours.
cards.short_summary: Free public museum galleries on the UT campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The McClung Museum states that museum admission is free and lists public visiting hours.
cards.source_title: Visit | McClung Museum of Natural History & Culture
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; the museum is closed for university holidays and home football games.

cards.title: See a UT Downtown Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Downtown Knoxville
cards.notes: Drop in to view the contemporary exhibitions, or time a visit with the gallery’s monthly First Friday opening.
cards.short_summary: University-curated contemporary art in downtown Knoxville.
cards.evidence_claim: All exhibitions and events at the UT Downtown Gallery are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: UT Downtown Gallery | The University of Tennessee, Knoxville
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; check the gallery page for current exhibition and First Friday details.

cards.title: Visit the Knoxville Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 1050 World's Fair Park Drive
cards.notes: Use the free general admission to move through the galleries and outdoor sculpture areas during posted museum hours.
cards.short_summary: Free admission to East Tennessee-focused visual art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Knoxville Museum of Art states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Knoxville Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; the museum posts hours and holiday or UT home-football closures on its visit page.

cards.title: Take a self-guided Emporium gallery lap
cards.subtitle: 100 S. Gay Street, downtown Knoxville
cards.notes: Browse the rotating gallery exhibitions and working artist studios at your own pace; exhibitions change every four weeks.
cards.short_summary: Free downtown galleries with frequently changing work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arts & Culture Alliance states that Emporium Center admission is free, visits are self-guided, and all ages are welcome.
cards.source_title: Visit the Emporium | Arts & Culture Alliance
cards.access_notes: Free admission and open to the public; confirm current gallery hours before going.

cards.title: Walk the Knoxville Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 2743 Wimpole Avenue, Knoxville
cards.notes: Follow the garden paths and stone-wall landscapes from dawn to dusk; donations are optional, not an entry requirement.
cards.short_summary: A year-round public garden walk with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Knoxville Botanical Garden says it does not charge admission and that its grounds are free and open to the public 365 days a year.
cards.source_title: FAQs | Knoxville Botanical Garden and Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Grounds are free and open to the public daily from dawn to dusk; donations are optional.

cards.title: Catch a WDVX Blue Plate Special
cards.subtitle: Visit Knoxville, downtown Knoxville
cards.notes: Attend a noon live-radio performance at Visit Knoxville on a Monday through Thursday or Saturday; bringing lunch is welcome.
cards.short_summary: A free live-music radio audience experience downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: WDVX states that its Blue Plate Special is always free to join and holds noon shows at Visit Knoxville Monday through Thursday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Free to attend; use the station calendar to verify performers and the current location before leaving.

cards.title: Walk the Fort Sanders history route
cards.subtitle: Fort Sanders, Knoxville
cards.notes: Download the free Fort Sanders tour, gather a few friends, and walk the route at a pace that suits the group.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced, downloadable neighborhood history walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Knoxville History Project offers a free, self-paced Fort Sanders walking tour download.
cards.source_title: Self-Guided Walking Tours | Knoxville History Project
cards.access_notes: The downloadable self-guided tour is free; use ordinary pedestrian safety and respect private property.

cards.entity_name: University of Tennessee Self-Guided Walking Tour
cards.title: Trace campus history on foot
cards.subtitle: University of Tennessee, Knoxville campus
cards.notes: Download the University of Tennessee route and use it for a self-paced walk between named campus history stops.
cards.short_summary: A free campus-history route you can take on your own schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Knoxville History Project offers a free, self-paced University of Tennessee walking tour download.
cards.source_title: Self-Guided Walking Tours | Knoxville History Project
cards.access_notes: The downloadable self-guided tour is free; follow campus access rules and use marked pedestrian routes.

cards.entity_name: Knoxville Women of the Suffrage Era Self-Guided Walking Tour
cards.title: Follow the suffrage-era walking tour
cards.subtitle: Downtown Knoxville
cards.notes: Download the suffrage-era route, choose a daylight window, and pause at the historic stops as the group moves through downtown.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided route focused on Knoxville suffrage history.
cards.evidence_claim: Knoxville History Project offers a free, self-paced Knoxville Women of the Suffrage Era walking tour download.
cards.source_title: Self-Guided Walking Tours | Knoxville History Project
cards.access_notes: The downloadable self-guided tour is free; visit in daylight and observe pedestrian signals at street crossings.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct UT Knoxville library and academic-support environments, selected for documented study features and access details.

cards.title: Quiet Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · fourth and fifth floors
cards.notes: Bring solo reading or writing to the carrels on Hodges’s quiet floors; the library lists about 125 seats and access for all users.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels in Hodges’s designated quiet-floor environment.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists Quiet Study Carrels on Hodges floors four and five as quiet study space with about 125 capacity and access for all.
cards.access_notes: Listed as access for all; located on Hodges Library floors four and five.

cards.title: Quiet Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · fourth and fifth floors
cards.notes: Use these tables when you need a quieter setting for notes or a laptop; UT Libraries identifies floors one, four, and five as quiet floors.
cards.short_summary: Quiet-floor tables for independent research and study.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists Quiet Study Tables on Hodges floors four and five as quiet research and study space, with access for all.
cards.access_notes: Listed as access for all; UT Libraries identifies floors one, four, and five as quiet floors.

cards.title: Group Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · third and sixth floors
cards.notes: Meet a small group at the carrels on Hodges’s third or sixth floor; the library labels the setting conversational and estimates about 55 seats.
cards.short_summary: Conversational carrels built around small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists Group Study Carrels on Hodges floors three and six as conversational study space with about 55 capacity and access for all.
cards.access_notes: Listed as access for all on Hodges Library’s third and sixth floors.

cards.title: Morgan Commons North
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · The Commons, second floor
cards.notes: Set up in this second-floor Commons area for research, study, or workstation use; UT Libraries describes it as conversational and about 75 capacity.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor Commons workspace with a conversational volume level.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists Morgan Commons North in Hodges’s second-floor Commons for research, study, and workstation use, with access for all.
cards.access_notes: Listed as access for all in The Commons on Hodges Library’s second floor.

cards.title: Graduate Commons Study Rooms - Small
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · Graduate Commons, rooms 131B and 131C
cards.notes: Graduate students can use these small rooms for a whiteboard session with up to about four people; bring a VolCard for swipe access.
cards.short_summary: Graduate-only small rooms with whiteboards for focused group work.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists three small Graduate Commons study rooms with whiteboards, about four-person capacity, VolCard access for graduate students, and first-come availability.
cards.source_title: Graduate Commons Study Rooms - Small - Hours
cards.access_notes: Graduate students must swipe a VolCard; rooms are not reservable and are first come, first served.

cards.title: Graduate Commons Study Room - Large
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · Graduate Commons, room 131A
cards.notes: Graduate students can gather around the whiteboard in this approximately six-seat room; UT Libraries says it can host a dissertation defense.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only six-seat room for group work and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists the large Graduate Commons study room as a six-seat space with a whiteboard, dissertation-defense capability, and VolCard access for graduate students.
cards.source_title: Graduate Commons Study Room - Large - Hours
cards.access_notes: Graduate students must swipe a VolCard; the room is not reservable and is first come, first served.

cards.title: Pendergrass Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Pendergrass Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine Library · rooms A113A, A113B, A113F, and A113G
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a project meeting or presentation practice; each documented room has a desktop, large display monitor, and whiteboards.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Pendergrass rooms with display and whiteboard equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries lists Pendergrass Study Rooms as conversational presentation and study spaces for about eight people, with a desktop, large display monitor, and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Listed as access for all. Online reservations can be made up to two weeks ahead, for a maximum of two hours per day.

cards.title: Vol Study Center
cards.subtitle: Strong Hall · room 102
cards.notes: Undergraduates can use the Strong Hall study space and ask about peer learning support; the center also documents free printing and snacks there.
cards.short_summary: Academic Success Center space with undergraduate study support.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Knoxville states that the Vol Study Center offers free resources for all undergraduate students, including study space, free printing, and snacks at Strong Hall room 102.
cards.access_notes: The page identifies Strong Hall room 102 as the main location and advises confirming availability because occasional closures can occur.

cards.entity_name: Study Tables at DeVine Music Library
cards.title: Study Tables at DeVine Music Library
cards.subtitle: DeVine Music Library · Natalie L. Haslam Music Center, G04
cards.notes: Choose the music library tables for a change of setting while working with music resources; the library’s current spaces listing identifies them as study tables.
cards.short_summary: Study tables inside UT’s George F. DeVine Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries’ current spaces listing includes Study Tables at DeVine Music Library as a study space.
cards.access_notes: DeVine Music Library is located in room G04 of the Natalie L. Haslam Music Center; consult the library listing for current availability.

cards.title: Study Lounge - Sixth Floor
cards.subtitle: Hodges Library · sixth floor
cards.notes: Head to Hodges’s sixth-floor study lounge for an alternate library work area; UT Libraries lists this named space among its current study locations.
cards.short_summary: A named study lounge on Hodges Library’s sixth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Libraries’ current spaces listing includes the Study Lounge - Sixth Floor at Hodges Library as a study space.
cards.access_notes: Located on the sixth floor of Hodges Library; consult the library listing for current availability.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing destinations on the Cumberland Avenue corridor at UT Knoxville’s north campus edge.

cards.title: University of Tennessee Student Union
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 1502 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Start here for the visitor-facing hub: enter the Student Union and use the second-floor Visitors Center as a documented campus-orientation stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus-facing starting point with the Visitors Center upstairs.
cards.evidence_claim: UT lists the Student Union at 1502 Cumberland Avenue and locates the Visitors Center on its second floor.
cards.source_title: Campus Tour Parking and Travel Plans
cards.access_notes: Visitors Center access and tour arrangements are described by UT Admissions; check its page before a visit.

cards.title: VolShop—Cumberland Avenue
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 1655 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Browse the official campus-store location when you need university apparel or gear; confirm product availability in person before making a purchase.
cards.short_summary: The official VolShop location directly on Cumberland Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Human Resources lists VolShop—Cumberland Avenue at 1655 Cumberland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases are optional; consult VolShop for current store information.

cards.title: New Here Coffee
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 1915 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use this named café stop for locally roasted coffee or pastries; it is inside Hub Knoxville, so look for the building entrance before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A café inside Hub Knoxville with coffee and pastries.
cards.evidence_claim: New Here Coffee says it is inside Hub Knoxville at 1915 Cumberland Avenue and serves locally roasted coffee and pastries.
cards.access_notes: The café publishes current daily hours on its official page; purchases are optional.

cards.title: Oscar's Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 1840 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Choose a pizza, calzone, sandwich, or salad from the posted menu, and use the restaurant’s online ordering page if pickup suits your plan.
cards.short_summary: A Cumberland Avenue restaurant with pizza, calzones, sandwiches, and salads.
cards.evidence_claim: Oscar's official ordering site lists 1840 Cumberland Avenue and menu categories including pizza, calzones, sandwiches, and salads.
cards.access_notes: Food requires purchase; the official ordering page displays current ordering and hours information.

cards.title: Gus's Good Times Deli
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Make this a sandwich stop and check the deli’s own site for its current menu and location details before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A named Cumberland Avenue deli focused on sandwiches.
cards.evidence_claim: Gus's Good Times Deli identifies itself as a deli on Cumberland Avenue and describes its Knoxville sandwich offering.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; verify current service details directly with the deli.

cards.title: Sunspot
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 2200 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a meal using the restaurant’s posted kitchen schedule; the site specifically describes vegetarian and carnivore options alongside its food service.
cards.short_summary: A Cumberland Avenue restaurant with a documented multicultural menu focus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sunspot lists 2200 Cumberland Avenue, kitchen hours, and describes food for vegetarians and carnivores.
cards.access_notes: Use the kitchen hours rather than bar hours; dining requires purchase.

cards.title: Ayres Hall
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — campus side of Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Pause at this named campus landmark beside the corridor and use the official parking map to orient yourself before continuing toward central campus.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed UT landmark on the campus side of Cumberland Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s official campus parking map labels Ayres Hall adjacent to Cumberland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is generally possible from public campus walkways; building access may be limited.

cards.title: Strong Hall
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — campus side of Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use this map-listed building as a visual waypoint when walking the eastern end of Cumberland Avenue near the campus boundary.
cards.short_summary: A named UT building visible from the Cumberland Avenue campus edge.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s official campus parking map labels Strong Hall near Cumberland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Use public sidewalks and observe posted building-access rules.

cards.title: Jessie Harris Building
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — campus side of Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Mark this named, map-listed building while following the corridor’s campus edge; refer to the official map for its position near the Student Union area.
cards.short_summary: A clearly labeled UT destination along the Cumberland Avenue edge.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s official campus parking map labels the Jessie Harris Building near Cumberland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Exterior access is from public campus routes; interior access depends on posted rules.

cards.title: Graduate Knoxville
cards.subtitle: Cumberland Avenue corridor — 1706 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Use the hotel’s named Cumberland Avenue frontage as a documented corridor waypoint when orienting between campus and the adjacent commercial blocks.
cards.short_summary: A named hotel directly on the Strip near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Admissions lists Graduate Knoxville at 1706 Cumberland Avenue and describes it as steps from the university and Neyland Stadium.
cards.source_title: Campus Tour Parking and Travel Plans
cards.access_notes: This card is for exterior wayfinding; lodging and any services require arrangements or purchase.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Volunteer rituals, symbols, and game-day practices tied to UT Knoxville.

cards.title: Bearing the Torch
cards.subtitle: Torchbearer Plaza, UT Knoxville
cards.notes: Read the Volunteer Creed on the Torchbearer statue plaque, then look for the annual senior Torchbearer recognition.
cards.short_summary: A senior honor rooted in UT’s creed of service and leadership.
cards.evidence_claim: UT states that select seniors are honored annually as Torchbearers for academic achievement and outstanding commitment to others.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies the Torchbearer statue at Circle Park; confirm ceremony details with UT before attending.

cards.title: Torch Night
cards.subtitle: UT Knoxville new-student and senior ceremony
cards.notes: If the ceremony is scheduled during your term, attend to see students use symbolic torches to mark arrival or farewell.
cards.short_summary: A torch ceremony connecting new Volunteers with graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: UT says Torch Night has declared new classes official members of the student body since 1925, with seniors also holding symbolic torches at the farewell ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony timing and attendance details vary; check UT’s current calendar.

cards.title: Painting The Rock
cards.subtitle: The Rock, UT Knoxville
cards.notes: Visit the painted Knox dolomite landmark to read current campus messages; use only university-approved painting guidance if participating.
cards.short_summary: A 97.5-ton campus message board layered in paint.
cards.evidence_claim: UT dates the Rock’s role as a campus communications hub to 1980 and describes it as a place for messages, announcements, sports hype, and proposals.
cards.access_notes: Viewing is straightforward; follow university rules and posted guidance before attempting to paint it.

cards.title: Wear Orange on Friday
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide UT Knoxville tradition
cards.notes: Plan an orange layer for Friday and join the university’s invitation for the Volunteer family to show school spirit.
cards.short_summary: A weekly orange-wearing ritual shared by the Volunteer community.
cards.evidence_claim: UT encourages members of the Volunteer family to wear orange every Friday and identifies Big Orange Friday as a tradition begun in 2013.
cards.access_notes: No special access is described; this is a voluntary spirit practice.

cards.title: Checker the Stadium
cards.subtitle: Neyland Stadium and Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center
cards.notes: For a designated checker game, use the seating-color guidance issued with the event to help create the orange-and-white pattern.
cards.short_summary: Fans coordinate clothing colors by section to create a giant checkerboard.
cards.evidence_claim: UT says fans began creating an orange-and-white checker pattern in Neyland Stadium for one football game each season in 2014, and have also checkered basketball games.
cards.access_notes: Participation in the in-venue display requires an event ticket and the current section-color instructions.

cards.entity_name: University Seal on Johnson-Ward Pedestrian Walkway
cards.title: Don’t Step on the Seal
cards.subtitle: Johnson-Ward Pedestrian Walkway, near Hodges Library
cards.notes: Find the seal beside Hodges Library and decide whether to honor the student warning by walking around it.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition attaches graduation luck to a sidewalk seal.
cards.evidence_claim: UT says students warn that walking across the university seal on Johnson-Ward Pedestrian Walkway means a student will not graduate in four years.
cards.access_notes: The source places the seal next to Hodges Library.

cards.title: Line Up for Vol Walk
cards.subtitle: Peyton Manning Pass to Neyland Stadium
cards.notes: Before a home football game, stand along the designated route to watch the team, Smokey, and band approach the stadium.
cards.short_summary: A pregame procession that brings the football team through campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT states that before every home game the football team walks down Peyton Manning Pass, led by Smokey and Davy Crockett, while fans line the route.
cards.access_notes: Arrive before kickoff and follow event-day crowd-management instructions.

cards.title: Spot the Vol Navy
cards.subtitle: Tennessee River by Neyland Stadium
cards.notes: From a lawful riverside or stadium-area viewpoint on game day, look for boats flying UT colors near the stadium.
cards.short_summary: A riverborne game-day tradition born from a 1962 boat trip.
cards.evidence_claim: UT says fans made boating to football games a tradition after radio broadcaster George Mooney traveled the Tennessee River to a Vols game by boat in 1962.
cards.access_notes: Use only lawful public viewing areas; boating requires appropriate planning and safety compliance.

cards.title: Smokey Leads the Entrance
cards.subtitle: Neyland Stadium home football games
cards.notes: Watch the pregame entrance to see Smokey lead the Vols through the band’s T, then look for him on touchdown sidelines.
cards.short_summary: UT’s live bluetick mascot leads a signature football entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: UT states that at every home football game Smokey leads the Vols through a T formed by the Pride of the Southland Band and runs the sidelines after touchdowns.
cards.access_notes: Seeing the entrance inside Neyland Stadium requires a ticket; follow venue policies.

cards.title: Sing “Rocky Top”
cards.subtitle: Pride of the Southland Band tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the band’s rendition at a UT event and join the crowd only where participation is invited and appropriate.
cards.short_summary: A song adopted into Volunteer event culture through the marching band.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s Torchbearer magazine states that the Pride of the Southland Band first played “Rocky Top” at halftime of the Tennessee–Alabama game on October 21, 1972, and that it became one of UT’s beloved songs.
cards.access_notes: Event access depends on the venue; the source documents the tradition’s history rather than a public performance schedule.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Tennessee-Knoxville, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first weekend that starts with campus landmarks and learning spaces, then stretches into downtown Knoxville parks and public gathering places.

cards.title: Start among the seasonal plantings
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • 2506 Jacob Drive
cards.notes: Begin with a slow loop through the named garden collections. Bring water, follow posted paths, and use the visit to get oriented beyond the central campus.
cards.short_summary: A free, all-season botanical stop on the UT Institute of Agriculture campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Gardens, Knoxville is part of the UT Institute of Agriculture, is open in all seasons, and is free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden; check the official garden calendar for program-specific details.

cards.title: Meet at the Torchbearer
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning • Entrance to Circle Park
cards.notes: Pause at the statue and read the Volunteer Creed on site. Use the plaza as a clear meeting point before continuing toward the museum and the Hill.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus landmark at Circle Park’s entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Torchbearer Plaza is an on-campus outdoor location at Circle Park’s entrance, and the statue has represented UT’s official symbol since 1968.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; be considerate of any scheduled campus events using the space.

cards.entity_name: McClung Museum of Natural History & Culture
cards.title: Browse a gallery at McClung
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday • 1327 Circle Park Drive
cards.notes: Choose one current exhibition and give it unhurried attention. Register ahead if requested, and confirm the museum is not closed for a holiday or home football game.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum with natural history and culture exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The McClung Museum offers free admission; regular hours are Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with closures for university holidays and home football games.
cards.source_title: Visit | McClung Museum of Natural History & Culture
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; advanced registration is preferred. Confirm hours and football-game closures before going.

cards.title: Climb the Hill to Ayres Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • The Hill
cards.notes: Approach from the north-side plaza and take in the building’s checkerboard detail. Keep the visit to public exterior areas unless you have a university reason to enter.
cards.short_summary: UT’s landmark academic building, completed in 1921.
cards.evidence_claim: Ayres Hall, completed in 1921, is a campus landmark and is used by UT’s College of Arts and Sciences.
cards.access_notes: Use public outdoor approaches and comply with building access rules.

cards.title: Settle into Hodges for a reset
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Heart of campus
cards.notes: Pick either a quiet-study or group-study floor, then make a short plan for the week. Use the Learning Commons for campus research or technology help as needed.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library with designated quiet and group-study floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Hodges Library houses UT Libraries’ major collections and services; its floors include designated quiet-study and group-study areas.
cards.source_title: About the John C. Hodges Library
cards.access_notes: During semesters the library has extended hours; check the live library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Union as your evening base
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening • 1502 Cumberland Avenue
cards.notes: Find the information desk, browse the building, and identify a comfortable public place to regroup. Check current facility hours, especially during breaks and holidays.
cards.short_summary: A central campus gathering place with published weekend facility hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union lists academic-year Saturday hours of 7 a.m.–10 p.m. and says its schedule changes with the academic calendar and special closures.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year Saturday hours are 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; verify special, break, holiday, and game-day hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the paths at World's Fair Park
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning • 1060 World's Fair Park Drive
cards.notes: Take the paved paths around the lake and festival lawns, then pause at the Sunsphere and amphitheater. Stay on marked paths and check weather before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A 10-acre downtown park with fair-era landmarks and walking paths.
cards.evidence_claim: World's Fair Park is a City of Knoxville park at 1060 World's Fair Park Drive, adjacent to the Sunsphere and other downtown cultural sites.
cards.source_title: World's Fair Park - City of Knoxville
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; confirm any weather or event-related restrictions before going.

cards.title: Check the Sunday-market alternative
cards.subtitle: Sunday midday • Market Square
cards.notes: If visiting during the May–October season, look for the producer-only market on its scheduled Wednesday or Saturday. Treat it as a browse-and-orient stop; purchases are optional.
cards.short_summary: A recurring open-air farmers market in downtown Market Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The Market Square Farmers' Market is a producer-only open-air market held Wednesdays and Saturdays from May through October.
cards.access_notes: This recurring market is scheduled Wednesday and Saturday, not Sunday; confirm the current listing and weather before planning around it.

cards.title: Pause in Market Square
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • Between Wall and Union avenues
cards.notes: Use the square and adjacent Krutch Park as a downtown waypoint. Look at the old Market House bell and suffrage monument, then check the city calendar for public events.
cards.short_summary: A downtown public square with event space, a fountain, and nearby Krutch Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Square lies between Wall and Union avenues, is adjacent to Krutch Park, and hosts special events, live music series, and seasonal farmers markets.
cards.source_title: Market Square Info - City of Knoxville
cards.access_notes: Outdoor civic space; event setups and seasonal programming may affect access.

cards.title: Close with a historic-campus loop
cards.subtitle: Sunday late afternoon • The Hill
cards.notes: Walk by South College from public paths and compare it with nearby Ayres Hall. Use the university’s historic-building guide to add context without entering restricted spaces.
cards.short_summary: A preserved historic building on the Hill, near Ayres Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: South College remains on its original site on the Hill and originally served as a dormitory and campus armory for East Tennessee University.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; do not assume interior access.

warnings: The farmers market is a Wednesday/Saturday activity, so it is included as a seasonal alternate rather than a literal Sunday stop. Check current university, museum, and city schedules before visiting.
